Companion.//: The one promoted turn intent (docs/LANGUAGE_ORGAN.md, Phase 2). Enabled for normal use on the controlled experiment's evidence: flag off, 0/3 clarifying questions on the canonical ambiguous-pronoun case; flag on, 3/3. Every other intent stays shadow-only.
Companion.//rendererShadow: docs/RENDERER_SHADOW.md — the run-1c renderer, served as the Ollama model renderer-shadow (merged+GGUF, revalidated). Enabled=false is the complete rollback; if the model is absent, observations and canary renders fall back silently and turns never notice.

RendererShadow.ModelVersion: run-1c merged+GGUF q8_0 via Ollama (layer 54e76dd5; merged from adapter 4732591a on base aa8e7253; revalidated 2026-08-24)
RendererShadow.//numgpu: 0 pins the renderer to CPU in Ollama so the chat model is never evicted from a small GPU; remove on machines with VRAM for both.
RendererShadow.//canary: User-scoped canary (RENDERER_SHADOW.md §8): this user's eligible turns DISPLAY run-1c, production is instant fallback. Clearing CanaryUserId is the one-setting rollback to the production renderer.

Api.//: Local API security. Binds to loopback by default; CORS is an explicit allow-list.
Api.//auth: AuthEnabled true requires a token (Authorization: Bearer, X-Companion-Key, or ?access_token=).
Api.//token: Leave Token empty to auto-generate one on first startup (saved to .companion-api-token next to the DB).

Models.//roles: Each job can use its own model. Extraction/Summarizer are optional and fall back to Chat. Reranker/TaskAuditor fall back to Summarizer; Safety falls back to Extraction. ToolPlanner (the executive that decides what to look up before she answers) falls back to Extraction then Chat — best served by a small instruction-following model, e.g. a 3B instruct at Temperature 0.1.
Models.//vision: Optional: add a 'Vision' block (e.g. Model 'llama3.2-vision') to enable /image.
Models.//transcription: Optional: add a 'Transcription' block pointing at a Whisper server to enable /transcribe.
Models.//speech: Optional: add a 'Speech' block pointing at a TTS server (OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech) to enable /speak.

Chat.//completion: AutoContinue resumes a reply cut off by the token limit (safe). CompletionCheck also asks a small model whether a self-stopped reply is done — powerful but only as good as that model; leave off until yours is trusted.
Chat.//completioncheck: Off by default because it was measured doing harm: a qwen2.5:3b judge kept declaring a finished reply unfinished, and one ordinary turn ran 5 rounds over 277s, concatenating four complete answers with four sign-offs. A structural sign-off check now overrules it, but the judge only earns its keep with a model that can actually make the call.
Chat.//logging: LogPayloads logs the full prompt + reply for this endpoint at Information level (also set Logging:LogLevel:Companion to Information to see it).

Reranker.//: Optional second-pass memory relevance judge. Small/fast is best; omit to reuse Summarizer.

Safety.//: Optional privacy classifier for durable derived memory. Omit to reuse Extraction.

TaskAuditor.//: Optional completion auditor for long deliverables. Omit to reuse Summarizer.

Speech.//: Kokoro has far more natural prosody than Piper. Pull it once: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/models/speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX  — other voices: af_bella, af_nicole, af_sky, bf_emma…

Safety.//: The reply gate: reads what she is about to say and decides whether it should be said. Everything else that inspects a reply checks its SHAPE; this is the only thing that reads its meaning.
Safety.//mode: Shadow judges every reply and records the verdict while changing nothing. Enforce replaces a refused reply with Replacement. Shadow first, always: a gate whose false-positive rate has never been measured should not be deciding what she may say, and reading /diagnostics/shadow?subject=safety.gate is how you measure it.
Safety.//failopen: It always fails open. A missing, slow or broken safety model lets the reply through - a gate that can end a conversation is worse than no gate.
Safety.//model: Uses the Safety chat role, which falls back to Extraction, so turning this on needs no extra model on the roster.
Safety.Replacement: I'd rather not take that anywhere. Ask me something else?

CognitiveModels.//: Small specialist ONNX models that make one judgment each, run in-process on the CPU. All OFF by default and all optional: every one improves on a heuristic that still works, so a missing model means the old behaviour and a log line, never a failure. See docs/SPECIALIST_MODELS.md.
CognitiveModels.//directory: Relative paths resolve next to the database, so models travel with the data rather than the binaries.
CognitiveModels.//required: Required true turns 'fall back quietly' into 'fail at startup' for that one model.
CognitiveModels.//get: Fetch the weights with tools/get-models.ps1. They are not committed.
CognitiveModels.//rerank: RerankMemories is separate from Reranker:Enabled on purpose — loading a model so it can be measured in shadow is a different decision from putting it in the path of every turn. It is off because it has not earned it: on the resolution set the cross-encoder and the keyword score are level at 11/12.
CognitiveModels.//capture: Capture records what the heuristics said about real sentences, so the corpus a model is judged on stops being entirely synthetic. It needs no model, which makes it the one measurement that is useful today. It writes user text into the telemetry store, so it runs only on turns already allowed to produce durable memory, drops the text (keeping the verdict) when SecretDetector fires, and is a separate switch from ShadowMode. Harvest with training/cognition/harvest.py.

World.//: A place she lives in, if she has one. Empty Url = no world, and nothing here runs. See docs/WORLD.md.
World.//url: The AvaWorld server's wire, e.g. ws://192.168.1.20:8738 (the port ABOVE the game client's).
World.//token: The same secret as the world's .avaworld-token, or its AVAWORLD_TOKEN.
World.//boundary: She holds a connection, never a model: no places are stored here, and the world re-advertises them on every connect.
World.//roam: Roam false keeps the connection and perception but stops her moving herself — useful for watching what she would do.

Outreach.//: Let her reach out on her own (push notifications via ntfy). Pick a hard-to-guess topic, set NtfyUrl to e.g. https://ntfy.sh/companion-<random>, and subscribe to the same topic in the ntfy app. Empty = off. See docs/OUTREACH.md.

Identity.//: Who the companion is (separate from how it behaves). Change by talking ("your name is Ava", "you're a woman") or via PUT /identity. Only Name/Gender/Pronouns are read; relationship framing belongs in the persona (PUT /persona or "set your persona to …").
Identity.Name: Ava

Personality.//: Default personality preset: seductive. Users can switch by talking or via PUT /personality.
